title: Facebook Ad Sizes 2026: Specs + What Really Runs | Sprites
summary: Every Facebook and Instagram ad size for 2026 — feed, stories, reels, carousel — plus which shapes advertisers actually ship, with real examples of each.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- **Produce 1080 × 1350 (4:5) first.** Portrait is roughly two thirds of what advertisers ship.
- **Add 1080 × 1920 (9:16)** for Stories and Reels — keep text out of the top and bottom ~14%.
- **1080 × 1080 (1:1)** for carousel cards, about a fifth of live creative.
- **1200 × 628 (1.91:1)** is now a minority shape, mostly right column and in-stream.


## The spec table


Placement Ratio Pixels Notes


Feed image / video 4:5 or 1:1 1080 × 1350 / 1080 × 1080 4:5 takes the most screen without cropping


Stories & Reels 9:16 1080 × 1920 Keep text clear of top and bottom ~14%


Carousel card 1:1 1080 × 1080 Same ratio on every card in the set


Right column 1.91:1 1200 × 628 Desktop only, small surface


In-stream video 16:9 → 1:1 1280 × 720+ Captions essential, sound off by default


## What advertisers actually ship


Specs tell you what is allowed. These are live ads at each ratio, so you can see what the shape does in a feed:


**9:16** — 338 × 600. Stories and Reels: full screen, text in the middle third. **4:5** — 480 × 600. The feed default: maximum height without a crop. **1:1** — 360 × 360. Square, the carousel and legacy feed shape. **16:9** — 640 × 360. Landscape, now mostly in-stream and right column.


Sprites' proprietary marketing agent reads the split as roughly **two thirds portrait, a fifth square, an eighth landscape** . If you produce one shape, produce 4:5. If you produce two, add 9:16. Landscape is an accommodation, not a default.


## Three sizing mistakes that cost delivery


- **One asset for every placement.** A 1:1 stretched into Stories wastes half the screen and reads as an afterthought.
- **Text in the safe zone.** On 9:16, the profile row and CTA eat the top and bottom — burned-in captions land under the interface.
- **Upscaled exports.** Meta compresses hard; anything below 1080 on the long edge arrives soft in the feed.
